examples.title: Worked application: Functional dependencies and normalisation
steps: A functional dependency X→Y means that each value of X determines exactly one value of Y within the relation. Normalisation uses dependencies to reduce update, insertion, and deletion anomalies. First normal form addresses repeating groups/non-atomic values; higher forms impose additional dependency conditions. Decomposition should aim for lossless joins and, where possible, dependency preservation.

A guaranteed reduction in every query cost
practiceQuestions.explanation: Repeated facts can produce inconsistent updates; normalisation separates facts according to their dependencies.

examples.title: Worked application: Indexes and query plans
steps: An index is an auxiliary structure that can reduce the work needed to locate rows, at the cost of storage and maintenance during writes. A query plan describes the operations the database expects to perform. Index usefulness depends on selectivity, query predicates, ordering, joins, statistics, and the optimiser’s cost estimates; adding indexes indiscriminately can slow writes.
